summary: Georgia lookout list places a tower named leesburg in Lee County; no source gives its history or describes the site today.

evidence.supports: List row for leesburg: Lee County, coordinates, an elevation of 260 with no unit stated, and the codes BLL-41131 and gfc-320
The list's names for towers numbered 73 and above are its own creation; this entry is number 183
evidence.quote: (For towers 73 and above, names are my creation.)

evidence.supports: The list marks some entries as historical
The list's Google map was revised on March 22, 2016
The list explains BLL-nnn codes: GFC provided coordinates for 118 towers
The list explains gfc-nnn codes: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers
evidence.quote: an older GFC list described the locations of 203 towers (gfc-nnn)

notes_for_editor: Only source is the tnlandforms.us Georgia list. Two web searches and one more check found no build, staffing, fire or fate history for a Leesburg tower. The Eastern U.S. Lookouts page titled Leesburg is a Florida tower (Lake County), not this one. The NHLR Georgia index (29 registered lookouts, read from the cache) and the Eastern U.S. Lookouts Georgia directory list no Leesburg tower. The list gives the elevation with no unit; the record's 79.2 m assumes feet (260 ft). Search leads that are not evidence of a lookout: a 97.5 m structure in Leesburg in an FCC antenna database, listed as owned by Lee County and apparently a communications tower; a Firetower Road in Leesburg that appears in real-estate listings. Story is about 155 words because the evidence is thin. Fact-check 2026-10-21: the page explains the BLL-nnn and gfc-nnn codes, which the story now says.
